captions: Some careers deliver projects.

Others leave behind a standard, a method
— and the people who carry it forward.

Honorary Fellow (PCI): conferred by the
Board of an independent professional body,

in recognition of distinguished
contribution, leadership and service.

Your name, on PCI's own public
registry — checkable at source.

The Project Controls Institute is
an independent professional body —
a Delaware Non-Stock Corporation —

built to give the discipline a shared
standard, an independent credential
and a professional home for the AI era.

Its published Body of Knowledge sets thirteen
domains and sixty-one knowledge areas.

Its framework is developed with
reference to ISO/IEC 17024,

and PCI states plainly that it is
not currently accredited by ANAB,
IAS or any ISO/IEC 17024 body.
What it has is a registry anyone can check.

It involves no examination. The record is
the evidence, and the Board weighs it.

It is separate from PCI's examined
certifications — PCL-AI, PFL-AI and PML-AI.
Every application is considered individually,

and recognition is conferred
solely at the Board's discretion.

If you have led teams, shaped standards,
taught, published or governed —

in project controls, cost control,
finance, project management or a closely
related discipline — you may apply.

From construction and energy to
technology, aviation, project
finance, government and academia:
wherever leadership shapes outcomes,
your contribution counts.

The floor is eight years' experience,
three of them at managerial level —

leading teams, functions,
programmes or budgets.

The bar is higher: a demonstrable
record of distinguished contribution.

Meeting the criteria does
not guarantee recognition.

PCI charges no nomination,
assessment or credential fee.

Optional extras, such as attending an
awards ceremony, are charged separately
and play no part in the decision.
Recognition is awarded solely on merit.

One application: your profile,
résumé, career history and evidence,
reviewed confidentially by the Board.
You need no sponsor to be considered.
You put your own record forward.

The Board then assesses it against
published criteria, on the evidence —
and does so confidentially.

Those recognised are entered
on PCI's own public registry:
checkable at source by anyone,
labelled honorary, never a passed examination.

If recognised, you may also be given
access to the PCI student portal and
the Institute's learning resources —

video lectures, course material
and the simulation lab.

The same terms may extend to study through
Certuvo, PCI's official preparation platform,

and invitations to selected PCI AI events
— all subject to current programme terms.

Tell the Board which discipline
your contribution aligns to:

project controls, project
finance or project management.

Optional, and it confers
no examined certification.

If your work has outlasted the projects it
was done on, it deserves to be recognised.

Apply for the Board's
consideration at pciai.org.
Questions to Members@pciai.org.
